To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

laminin-containing basement membrane-like structures associated with tumour cell membranes are present in only 27% of the rectal adenocar-cinomas examined, that their presence is associated with a low grade of tumour differentiation, but not with tumour progression through the bowel wall, and that the presence of such basement membranes is associated with a reduced incidence in the development of distant metastases, and with an improved survival.

(1) in normal human large intestine, laminin and fibro-nectin are found in basement membranes; (2) in rectal carcinoma, laminin is found in basement membranes only when the tumour is well differentiated and (3) the presence of laminins in the tumour basement membrane is associated with a reduced incidence and survival of patients with distant metastases.

the presence of a tumour cell basement membrane-like structure, containing laminin but not collagen IV, is correlated with low histologic grade, but not with tumour stage or metastases, and that the presence of stromally located fibronectin is not related to any of the above factors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a possible role for laminin in the control of metastatic behaviour of human rectal adenocarinomas.

the development of a novel, non-invasive imaging technique that will enable the identification of patients with rectal cancer who are likely to have distant metastases and who may therefore be candidates for adjuvant chemotherapy.
the development and use of new techniques for the detection and measurement of tumour markers in human cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of basement membrane-like laminin staining in rectal adenomas correlates with a reduced incidence and delayed development of distant metastases, but not with tumour grade or stage.
laminin, unlike fibronectin, is a marker for well-differentiated tumour cells in rectal adenomas, but is of limited value in predicting the development of metastases.

laminin-containing basement membrane material is present in a high proportion of well-differentiated tumour cells and this is associated with a low incidence of distant metastasis and a good patient survival.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
laminin-containing basement membrane-like material in tumour cells is associated with low histological grades and a reduced incidence of metastases and death from the disease.
